p000.lead: Deity, God, reality, personality, and the Trinities: reading the twelve sections of the Foreword through tables and the text itself.

p000.foot.text: Indited by an Orvonton Divine Counselor, Chief of the Corps of Superuniverse Personalities assigned to portray on Urantia the truth concerning the Paradise Deities and the universe of universes

p000.s0.h: Introduction — Why Is There a Foreword?
p000.s0.b0: The Foreword is the first thing anyone meets on opening The Urantia Book. Yet it does not begin with a story. It begins as a guide to terms, in which a Divine Counselor of Orvonton defines in advance the words that will be used later. The reason is stated plainly in the first paragraph: in human minds there is great confusion about the meaning of words like God, divinity, and deity, and still more uncertainty about the relationships of the divine personalities called by those names.

p000.s0.b1.q: Because of this conceptual poverty associated with so much ideational confusion, I have been directed to formulate this introductory statement

p000.s0.b2: The revelators knew well how narrow human language is. So they state that they will use existing English words wherever possible and introduce new terms only when no suitable word can be found. The Foreword feels difficult partly because it deals with the highest realities of the universe, but also because it sets up at once the conceptual framework for all 196 papers that follow. It is therefore less a text to read once and finish than a map to return to whenever an unfamiliar concept appears.

p000.s0.b3.q: This Foreword is not, therefore, a finished statement within itself

p000.s0.b4: The Foreword also begins by telling us where we are in the universe. Urantia is a planet in the local universe of Nebadon; Nebadon belongs to Orvonton, one of the seven superuniverses; the seven superuniverses circle the central universe of Havona; and at its heart lies Paradise. Keeping this address in mind makes everything that follows much clearer.

head: Unit
Description
rows: The planet we live on—one of the many inhabited planets of Nebadon
The local universe ruled by Michael, a Creator Son
The seventh superuniverse, which includes Nebadon; its capital is Uversa
The central universe of Havona and the seven superuniverses—the now organized and inhabited creation
The grand universe together with the still-mobilizing universes of outer space
The center of all things, the dwelling place of the eternal God

p000.s1.h: I. Deity and Divinity — Telling the Words for God Apart
p000.s1.b0: The first distinction the Foreword draws is between Deity and divinity. Deity may be personalized as God, but it also exists in prepersonal and superpersonal ways that man cannot fully comprehend. The quality that characterizes Deity is unity, and creatures best comprehend this unifying quality as divinity.
p000.s1.b1: Deity functions on seven levels. The first three are Deity as it already exists in eternity; the later levels are Deity as it is disclosed in time and space through creation and evolution.
p000.s1.b3: Divinity appears in three ways, depending on how we experience it. This threefold distinction returns again and again whenever the book speaks of truth, beauty, and goodness.

p000.s1.b4.q: Divinity is creature comprehensible as truth, beauty, and goodness; correlated in personality as love, mercy, and ministry; disclosed on impersonal levels as justice, power, and sovereignty.

p000.s2.b0: The Foreword strictly distinguishes Deity from God. Deity may or may not be personal, but God always denotes personality. So whenever we meet the word “God” in The Urantia Book, we should ask which personality it refers to. The Foreword sets out seven uses.

p000.s2.b1.q: The term God always denotes personality.

head: Name
Role
Nature
rows: Creator, Controller, and Upholder (the Universal Father)
Co-ordinate Creator, Spirit Controller, and Spiritual Administrator (the Eternal Son)
Conjoint Actor, Universal Integrator, and Mind Bestower (the Infinite Spirit)
The actualizing or evolving God of time and space
Deity personality anywhere actually functioning in time and space
The eventuating God of supertime and transcended space
The experientializing God of transcended superpersonal values and divinity meanings

p000.s2.b3: The Universal Father also relates to us on three levels. On the prepersonal level he functions through Father fragments such as the Thought Adjusters; on the personal level, in the experience of created beings; on the superpersonal level, in the existence of absonite beings. That the Adjuster indwelling our minds is the Father in the first of these ways is the starting point of personal religion.
p000.s3.h: III. The First Source and Center — Seven Co-ordinate Absolutes
p000.s3.b0: The starting point of all reality is the First Source and Center, the Universal Father. The Foreword explains that total, infinite reality exists in seven phases, as seven co-ordinate Absolutes.

p000.s3.b1.q: Total, infinite reality is existential in seven phases and as seven co-ordinate Absolutes

head: Absolute
Brief description
rows: Source of the material universe; the nonpersonal pattern
The unifier that co-ordinates the tension between the two
Undeified potential—the mechanizer of the universes

p000.s3.b3: The Foreword tells how these seven “differentiated” as if it were a story in time. Of course in eternity there is no before and after; the sequence is given so that finite minds can grasp it. Through his free will the I AM achieved liberation from unqualified infinity, producing the first divinity-tension, which the Universal Absolute resolves. As the Son was differentiated from the Father and Paradise appeared, the Infinite Spirit and the central universe of Havona also appeared.
p000.s3.b4: The key point to remember here is that everything springs from the Father’s will. The universe did not begin as a machine of chance or necessity, but from the free choice of a loving person.
p000.s4.h: IV. Universe Reality — How Reality Is Divided
p000.s4.b0: Reality originates in the infinite volition of the Universal Father and appears in three fundamental phases.

head: Phase
Range
rows: From the energy domains of the nonpersonal to the presence of the Unqualified Absolute
From the lowest finite personality to the highest infinite, even to the presence of the Deity Absolute
The vast domain between the two—embraced in the Universal Absolute

p000.s4.b2: From the viewpoint of time and space, reality is further divided into actual and potential, absolute and subabsolute, and so on. The Foreword’s example is striking: the Eternal Son is an absolute spiritual actuality, while mortal man is very largely an unrealized spiritual potentiality. Our lives are the process of turning that potential into actuality.
p000.s4.b3: Paradise is often misunderstood in this section. Paradise is the source of the material universe and the center of gravity, but it is not a creator, and it is not a person.
p000.s5.h: V. Personality Realities — What a Human Being Is Made Of
p000.s5.b0: The section of the Foreword that touches our lives most directly is the fifth, on personality. Personality is a level of deified reality, and it never arises on its own. It is the Father’s gift.

p000.s5.b1.q: Personality is never spontaneous; it is the gift of the Paradise Father.

p000.s5.b2: The Foreword then lays out human experience on Urantia on five levels. It is no exaggeration to say that this table condenses the view of man found throughout the whole book.

head: Level
What it is
Destiny
rows: The material or physical organism; a living electrochemical mechanism
The thinking, perceiving, and feeling mechanism; grows upward through worship and wisdom
Becomes the mother of the soul
The indwelling Thought Adjuster; an immortal, prepersonal spirit
Destined to fuse with the personality
A morontia reality acquired by experience; the spirit is its father and the mind its mother
The one changeless reality in an otherwise ever-changing experience

p000.s5.b4: The way the soul comes into being is especially beautiful. When a person chooses to do the will of the Father in heaven, a new reality is born between the indwelling spirit and the material mind.

p000.s5.b5.q: As a mortal creature chooses to “do the will of the Father in heaven,” so the indwelling spirit becomes the father of a new reality in human experience.

p000.s5.b6: Here a new term appears: morontia. Morontia designates the vast level between the material and the spiritual, and the Foreword likens it to a woven cloth whose warp is spiritual and whose woof is physical. Our soul is just such a morontia reality, and life on the mansion worlds after death is morontia life.
p000.s6.h: VI. Energy and Pattern — Four Circuits
p000.s6.b0: The sixth section sorts out the four drawing powers that move the universe. Whether a thing is personal, spirit, mind, or matter depends on which circuit it responds to.
p000.s6.b2: The Foreword also warns in advance that words like energy, force, and power are used differently from their everyday definitions; the poverty of language forces one word to carry several meanings. It then states that pattern can configure energy but cannot control it, and that the sole control of energy-matter is gravity.

p000.s6.b3.q: Gravity is the sole control of energy-matter.

p000.s7.h: VII. The Supreme Being — The Evolving God
p000.s7.b0: The seventh section introduces one of the most distinctive teachings of The Urantia Book. Deity is of two kinds: existential Deity, which exists eternally, like the Father, the Son, and the Spirit; and experiential Deity, which is being actualized as the universe grows, like God the Supreme, God the Ultimate, and God the Absolute.

p000.s7.b2.q: The essence of Deity is eternal, but only the three original persons of Deity are unqualifiedly eternal.

p000.s7.b3: The Supreme Being is not a direct creator but a synthetic co-ordinator of all creature-Creator activity, and when finally actualized he will constitute the eternal fusion of the finite and the infinite. This teaching means a great deal to us. The choices we make and the experience we gather in time do not vanish; they actually contribute to the actualization of the evolving God.
p000.s8.h: VIII. God the Sevenfold — Seven Ways He Draws Near to Us
p000.s8.b0: A finite creature cannot approach the infinite Father directly. So the Father has provided a sevenfold way of approach to Deity.

p000.s8.b1.q: To atone for finity of status and to compensate for creature limitations of concept, the Universal Father has established the evolutionary creature’s sevenfold approach to Deity

head: Order
Deity personality
Relation to us
rows: Father of the local universe—for us, Michael (Jesus)
Representatives of the Infinite Spirit who watch over the superuniverses
The evolving God of time and space
The final goal of the ascent

p000.s8.b3: The ascent begins with recognizing the divinity of the Creator Son, passes through the Ancients of Days and a Master Spirit, and at last reaches the Father on Paradise. In other words, for a person of Urantia the first step on the journey toward God is to know the Father through Jesus.
p000.s9.h: IX–X. God the Ultimate; God the Absolute
p000.s9.b0: Just as the Supreme Being evolves in the grand universe, God the Ultimate eventuates in the domains that transcend time and space. The Foreword contrasts the two concisely.

p000.s9.b1.q: The Supreme is the Trinity unification comprehended by finite beings; the Ultimate is the unification of the Paradise Trinity comprehended by absonite beings.

p000.s9.b2: God the Absolute lies further still. He will be realized through the unification of the Absolute Trinity, and he is the goal of all superabsonite beings. The revelators deliberately hold back from speaking of this realm, frankly admitting that its reality goes beyond our concepts. This honesty is an attitude that runs through the whole Foreword.
p000.s10.b0: When the Father, in creating Havona, segregated his presence from infinite potential, the unrevealed infinite potential remained in the Unqualified Absolute and was encompassed by the Deity Absolute, and these two were bound together in the Universal Absolute.

head: Absolute
Character
A figurative way to understand it

p000.s10.b2: Why does the Universal Absolute matter? Because our very ability, as finite beings, to exist in an infinite cosmos depends on it.

p000.s10.b3.q: The finite can coexist in the cosmos along with the Infinite only because the associative presence of the Universal Absolute so perfectly equalizes the tensions

p000.s10.b4: And the Foreword concludes that these three are in the end one Absolute. On subinfinite levels they appear functionally distinct, but in infinity they are one.
p000.s11.b0: The last section deals with the Trinities. The eternal Paradise Trinity is existential and was inevitable. The two post-Havona Trinities, by contrast, are experiential and are still being actualized.

head: Trinity
Members
Nature
rows: The Universal Father · the Eternal Son · the Infinite Spirit
The Supreme Being · the Supreme Creator Personalities · the Architects of the Master Universe
God the Supreme · God the Ultimate · the Consummator of Universe Destiny

p000.s11.b2.q: Trinities are truths of relationship and facts of co-ordinate Deity manifestation.

p000.s11.b3: The philosophers of the universes postulate a “⟦Q 0:12.9⟧Trinity of Trinities⟦/Q⟧” embracing all of this, yet they confess that they cannot even envisage its personalization.
p000.s12.h: Acknowledgment — How the Revelation Was Written
p000.s12.b0: The close of the Foreword frankly explains how the revelation was written. Wherever possible, the revelators gave preference to the highest concepts humans had already expressed, and resorted to new expression only when those were inadequate. They selected more than one thousand human concepts from God-knowing mortals as the basis of the papers.
p000.s12.b1: Finally, they explain why truth can be conveyed however inadequate language may be.

p000.s12.b2.q: But we know that there dwells within the human mind a fragment of God, and that there sojourns with the human soul the Spirit of Truth

p000.s12.b3: This sentence is the key to reading the whole Foreword. Its terms are difficult, but we are not left to understand them alone. The Adjuster within us and the Spirit of Truth turn unfamiliar concepts into living truth. So there is no need to be discouraged if we do not understand all of the Foreword. It is a text that grows a little clearer each time we come back to it as we read through the book.
p000.s13.h: Conclusion — How to Read the Foreword

head: Tip
Explanation
rows: Do not try to grasp every term at once; just get hold of the overall structure (I–XII)
When an unfamiliar term comes up in the papers, come back to the Foreword to check it
The distinction between what exists eternally and what is being actualized unlocks many sentences
The distinction of body, mind, spirit, soul, and personality is the foundation of personal religion
After Part I, and again after the whole book, it will look entirely different

p001.lead: The God of all creation, and a person we can know and love: the paper in which The Urantia Book first introduces the Universal Father.

p001.foot.text: Presented by a Divine Counselor of Uversa

p001.s0.h: Introduction — Why Begin with the Father?
p001.s0.b0: If the Foreword lays out a map of terms, Paper 1 introduces the One at the center of that map. Before it describes the structure of the universe or the orders of celestial beings, The Urantia Book speaks of the **Universal Father**, because all things and beings come from him and the journey of every ascending creature leads back to him. The paper asks us to think of God first as a creator, then as a controller, and lastly as an infinite upholder.

p001.s0.b1.q: the God of all creation, the First Source and Center of all things and beings

p001.s0.b2: The God this paper portrays is no distant principle. The myriads of planetary systems were made to be inhabited by creatures who could know God, receive his affection, and love him in return, and the will creatures of universe upon universe have already set out on the long journey to attain the Father. So the opening of Paper 1 turns at once into a call addressed to us: be perfect, even as the Father in heaven is perfect.

p001.s0.b3.q: This is the true meaning of that divine command, “Be you perfect, even as I am perfect,” which ever urges mortal man onward and beckons him inward

p001.s0.b4: The perfection meant here is not perfection in the infinite sense. Mortals, starting out where they are and moving in their own way, can still reach the divine goal that God has set for them. This perfection is less a flawless state than a direction—the direction of endless growth.
p001.s1.h: I. The Father’s Name — What Matters More Than a Name
p001.s1.b0: God is called by many names throughout the universes: the First Source, the Universe Center, the Father of Fathers, the Paradise Father, and others. Yet the paper makes a striking claim: God has never revealed himself by name, only by nature. He makes himself known not through a title but through what he is.

head: Where
The name used
rows: Father of Fathers · Paradise Father · Havona Father · Spirit Father

p001.s1.b2: What, then, really matters? The paper’s answer is plain. Whatever name we use, the important thing is to know him and to long to become like him.

p001.s1.b3.q: The name he is given is of little importance; the significant thing is that you should know him and aspire to be like him.

p001.s1.b4: Nor does God impose formal worship or slavish service on anyone. Each person must, in his or her own heart, recognize, love, and freely worship him. This is why the paper calls **the affectionate dedication of the human will to doing the Father’s will** man’s choicest gift to God. Of all that we have, the only thing God does not already possess is our free choice.
p001.s2.h: II. The Reality of God — How Do We Know Him?
p001.s2.b0: God is primal reality in the spirit world, the source of truth in the mind spheres, and he overshadows all throughout the material realms. The paper states firmly that God is neither manlike nor machinelike. He is universal spirit, eternal truth, infinite reality, and father personality.
p001.s2.b1: How, then, do we know that God exists? Never by scientific experiment or by logical deduction. God can be realized only in the realms of human experience. The paper says that the presence of the Thought Adjuster dwelling within us is disclosed by three kinds of experience.

head: Experience
What it is
rows: The intellectual capacity for knowing God
The spiritual urge to find God
The personality craving to be like God — the wholehearted desire to do his will

p001.s2.b3.q: Those who know God have experienced the fact of his presence

p001.s2.b4: The surest evidence a believer can offer others, then, is not an argument but a life. The person who knows God carries in his or her own experience the only positive proof of the living God that one human being can give to another.
p001.s3.h: III. God is a Universal Spirit
p001.s3.b0: “⟦Q 1:3.1⟧God is spirit.⟦/Q⟧” This classic confession stands at the center of the third section. To be created “⟦Q 1:3.1⟧in his image⟦/Q⟧” does not mean that God has a body like ours; it means that Mystery Monitors sent from his presence dwell within us. Spirit is invisible to human eyes, yet it is entirely real.
p001.s3.b1: The section also explains, briefly, how survival works. A mind linked only to matter cannot survive death. But when a God-conscious mind becomes more and more spirit taught and spirit led, its spiritual potential is transformed into the morontia reality of the immortal soul. A mind that remains bound to matter to the end, by contrast, comes at last to personality extinction.
p001.s3.b2: This passage has very practical meaning for the life of faith. Survival does not depend on how much we know or how faithfully we keep religious rites. It depends on whether the mind accepts the leading of the spirit in the small choices we make each day. The Urantia Book therefore treats survival not as a question for some distant future but as one bound up with today’s decisions. Each time we choose honesty, choose kindness, choose trust over fear, the soul within us grows a little more.

head: Where the mind turns
The outcome
rows: It accepts the teaching and leading of the spirit
The morontia soul grows and survives death
It becomes ever more material and ends in personality extinction

p001.s3.b4: At the close of the section the Divine Counselor adds his own testimony. As one who came forth from the Eternal and has returned again and again to the presence of the Universal Father, he affirms that two great declarations are true.

p001.s3.b5.q: I know the truth of the great declarations: “God is spirit” and “God is love,” and these two attributes are most completely revealed to the universe in the Eternal Son.

p001.s4.h: IV. The Mystery of God — God Within Us
p001.s4.b0: Because God’s perfection is infinite, he remains forever a mystery. Yet the greatest mystery the paper names is not the stars or the vastness of the universe. It is the fact that divinity dwells within the minds of mortals.

p001.s4.b1.q: The physical bodies of mortals are “the temples of God.”

p001.s4.b2: The fragment of God within us is not yet ours by right of possession, but it is designed to become one with us if we survive. When our course on earth is run, the dust returns to the earth from which it came, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
p001.s4.b3: God, moreover, is no respecter of persons. The divine presence any creature enjoys is not limited by favoritism on God’s part, but only by that creature’s capacity to receive and discern spiritual realities. If we want to meet more of God, it is not God who must change; we must widen our capacity to receive him.
p001.s5.h: V–VI. Personality of the Universal Father; Personality in the Universe
p001.s5.b0: We must not let God’s infinity obscure his personality. The paper says that the Universal Father is the acme of divine personality, the origin and destiny of all personality throughout creation. God is both infinite and personal; he is an infinite personality.

p001.s5.b1.q: Personality, in the supreme sense, is the revelation of God to the universe of universes.

p001.s5.b2: This personal God takes part in our lives at the deepest level. His spirit is a real part of us, so that when we are afflicted he is afflicted, and when we triumph he triumphs in and with us. God is not an indifferent observer; he is a Father who shares what we go through.
p001.s5.b3: The sixth section sets out how differently people understand God. The same God appears as a cause, an idea, or a living person, depending on where one stands.

head: To
God is
rows: An idea · a hypothesis of unity
A person · the loving heavenly Father · a living spiritual experience

p001.s5.b5: The section also tells us who has shown God’s personality most clearly. Jesus of Nazareth attained the full realization of the potential of spirit personality in human experience, and his life of doing the Father’s will became man’s most real and ideal revelation of the personality of God. If we want to know what God is like, we can look at the life of Jesus.
p001.s6.h: VII. Spiritual Value of the Personality Concept
p001.s6.b0: The final section explains why the idea of a personal God matters so much. The concept of a personal God makes fellowship possible, encourages intelligent worship, and nurtures a refreshing trust. Impersonal things can interact, but they cannot have fellowship.
p001.s6.b1: For this reason the paper corrects a familiar image from mysticism. We do not become one with God the way a drop of water is lost in the ocean. We are united with him through personal communion and wholehearted conformity to his will, gradually taking on more and more of the divine nature.

head: Value
Its relation to personality
rows: Might be entertained apart from personality
Understandable only in relation to personality

p001.s6.b3.q: Only a person can love and be loved.

p001.s7.b0: Paper 1 is less a body of information about God than an invitation into a relationship with him. Its message can be gathered into three points. God is a person whom we can know and love. He already lives within us as spirit. And the one true gift we can offer him is our free choice to do his will.

head: Practice
The teaching behind it
rows: Pause once a day and become aware of the Father within
The mortal body is a temple of God
Facing a decision, ask, “What is the Father’s will?”
The dedication of our will is the choicest gift
Treat everyone you meet as a child of the same Father
God is no respecter of persons
Come to know God through the mirror of Jesus’ life
Jesus is the most real revelation of God’s personality

p001.s7.b2: After Paper 1, the papers that follow unfold in turn the nature of God (Paper 2), his attributes (Paper 3), and his relation to the universe and to the individual (Papers 4 and 5). If we read them with the picture from this first paper in mind—a Father who can be known and loved—we will sense that even the harder concepts ahead all point toward this one Person.
p002.lead: The paper that portrays what the infinite and perfect God is like in his justice and mercy, his love and goodness, and his truth and beauty.

p002.foot.text: Presented by a Divine Counselor acting by authority of the Ancients of Days on Uversa

p002.s0.h: Introduction — Where Do We See God’s Nature?
p002.s0.b0: If Paper 1 introduced God as a Father who can be known, Paper 2 looks at that Father’s **nature**—the character he possesses. It takes up in turn his infinity, his perfection, his justice, his mercy, his love, his goodness, and his truth and beauty. At the outset the author makes clear that the best window on the divine nature is not an abstract definition but the life of Jesus of Nazareth.
p002.s0.b1: At the same time the author frankly admits the limits of the task. The mortal mind has limited capacity, and human language is poor in the illustrations needed to portray divine values. The attempt is not futile, however, because the mortal mind is indwelt by the Adjuster and pervaded by the Spirit of Truth. Understanding God becomes possible, in the end, when the God within us helps.

head: Section
Aspect of God’s nature
The point in a line
rows: Beyond measure, yet he downsteps himself to draw near
His purpose never changes, and he shares in our imperfection
We reap what we sow, but justice is always tempered with mercy
Mercy is justice tempered by wisdom
God is love—the Adjuster is the proof
Truth, beauty, and goodness are unified in love

p002.s1.h: I. The Infinity of God — The Immeasurable One Draws Near
p002.s1.b0: The first section gathers the confessions of ancient scripture to show God’s infinity. God is fully self-conscious of his infinity and perfection; he is neither a cosmic accident nor a universe experimenter. The Universe Sovereigns may engage in adventure and the Constellation Fathers may experiment, but the Father sees the end from the beginning. For him there is no past or future; all time is present.

p002.s1.b1.q: No thing is new to God, and no cosmic event ever comes as a surprise

p002.s1.b2: Yet this very infinity shuts him off from direct personal communication with finite creatures. So the Father, in love, downsteps and dilutes his infinity to make a way of drawing near to his children. The paper names three such ways.

head: The way he draws near
How it works
rows: They partake of the flesh and blood of the planetary races and become one with us—as in the bestowal of Michael
The personalities of the Infinite Spirit
The seraphic hosts and other celestial intelligences minister to material beings
The impersonal Mystery Monitors come to indwell the minds of mortals

p002.s1.b4: The close of the section shows that infinity is not a concept that pushes us away. Man cannot encompass infinity, but the infinite Father fully comprehends and lovingly embraces all the finity of his children. That is why the words “⟦Q 2:1.11⟧In Him we live and move and have our being⟦/Q⟧” are literal truth. The Adjuster within us is itself a fragment of that infinity.
p002.s2.h: II. The Father’s Eternal Perfection — A Purpose That Never Changes
p002.s2.b0: God’s plans and purposes are like himself: eternal, perfect, and forever changeless. He does not repent of the wise purposes he first set. When the attitudes of his creatures change, his reactions may seem to change as well—but only on the surface. Beneath every outward manifestation flows the same unchanging purpose.
p002.s2.b1: What deserves special notice in this section is the character of that perfection. God’s perfection is not an assumed righteousness but the inherent **perfection of the goodness** of his nature. And the perfect One does not keep to himself. The whole scheme of life on the worlds of space is centered on lifting will creatures to share the Father’s perfection.

p002.s2.b2.q: God is neither self-centered nor self-contained; he never ceases to bestow himself upon all self-conscious creatures

p002.s2.b3: Remarkably, the perfect God, who cannot personally know imperfection as his own experience, nonetheless shares the consciousness of all the imperfectness experienced by the struggling creatures of the evolutionary universes. Our immaturity and our mistakes are not far removed from God; the Father actually participates in them. This is a comfort on the days we fail: we are not alone.
p002.s3.h: III. Justice and Righteousness — We Reap What We Sow
p002.s3.b0: God is righteous, and therefore he is just. His justice is not swayed by the deeds of his creatures; it shows no respect of persons and takes no gifts. So, the paper says, it is futile to make childish appeals to God in the hope of escaping the just consequences of his natural laws and spiritual mandates.

p002.s3.b1.q: whatsoever a man sows that shall he also reap

p002.s3.b2: The same paragraph at once restores the balance. Even in the reaping of the harvest of wrongdoing, divine justice is always tempered with mercy. The final result of wholehearted sin is annihilation, yet this is less a penalty imposed by God than the outcome of a creature becoming wholly unreal through the embrace of iniquity. And even that end is delayed until the ordained order of justice has been fully complied with.

head: Step
What happens
rows: At the dispensational or epochal adjudication of the realm—on Urantia, at the end of a planetary dispensation
Co-ordinate action of all tribunals, from the planetary council through the courts of the Creator Son to the tribunals of the Ancients of Days
The mandate of dissolution originates in the higher courts of the superuniverse after the indictment is confirmed
Carried out directly by the judges resident on the superuniverse headquarters
No resurrection—the personality ceases, and its experience is absorbed in the Supreme Being

p002.s3.b4: Beneath this section lies a simple principle. Undiluted evil and willful sin are inherently suicidal; what is unreal survives for a time only because of the tolerance of mercy. In the local universes the Creator Sons devote themselves to the rehabilitation of rebels, and the decree of dissolution is executed only when all such loving efforts are finally and forever rejected.
p002.s4.h: IV. The Divine Mercy — Justice Tempered by Wisdom
p002.s4.b0: The fourth section defines mercy not as the opposite of justice but as a form of it. God knows perfectly the natural weaknesses and environmental handicaps of his creatures, and the wisdom that grows from that knowledge tempers his justice. That is mercy.

p002.s4.b1.q: Mercy is simply justice tempered by that wisdom which grows out of perfection of knowledge and the full recognition of the natural weaknesses and environmental handicaps of finite creatures.

p002.s4.b2: Nor is God’s mercy something anyone has to coax out of him. The creature’s need alone is enough to ensure the full flow of the Father’s mercy. Because God knows all about his children, forgiveness is easy for him. The paper adds that the same principle holds between people.

p002.s4.b3.q: The better man understands his neighbor, the easier it will be to forgive him, even to love him.

head: Justice
Mercy
rows: The natural offspring of goodness and love
Follows the just consequences of law
Adapts justice to the situation of the evolving finite
Not a contravention of justice but its understanding interpretation

p002.s4.b5: God is never torn between justice and mercy, because infinite wisdom chooses the conduct that satisfies the demands of all his attributes perfectly, simultaneously, and equally. Unlike us, who are forever pulled between the two, God knows no conflict of attitudes. Together, eternal justice and divine mercy constitute what in human experience would be called **fairness**.
p002.s5.h: V. The Love of God — The Adjuster as Proof
p002.s5.b0: “⟦Q 2:5.1⟧God is love⟦/Q⟧.” His only personal attitude toward the affairs of the universe is therefore always a reaction of divine affection. The paper plainly calls it wrong to think that God is coaxed into loving his children by the sacrifices of his Sons or the intercession of others. The Father himself loves us, and it is in response to that affection that he sends the Adjusters.
p002.s5.b1: The author says that the supreme reason for loving God is the Adjuster patiently waiting within us. Though we cannot find God by searching, if we submit to the leading of the indwelling spirit, we will be guided step by step and life by life until at last we stand in the Father’s presence. The distance in space and the gulf of spiritual difference are great, but God has already bridged that gulf in his own way.

p002.s5.b2.q: The experience of loving is very much a direct response to the experience of being loved.

p002.s5.b3: The author’s own confession is striking. He says he would love God just as much if he were not so great and powerful, so long as he is good and merciful. We love the Father more for his nature than for his amazing attributes. Yet God’s love is not blind. It is an intelligent and farseeing parental affection that works in unity with divine wisdom.
p002.s5.b4: The paper also sums up where God’s love is shown. Its greatest **manifestation** to mortals is the bestowal of the Thought Adjusters; its greatest **revelation** is the bestowal life of Michael, who lived on earth the ideal spiritual life. And it is the indwelling Adjuster who individualizes that love to each human soul.

p002.s5.b5.q: God is love, but love is not God.

p002.s6.h: VI. The Goodness of God — He Loves as a Father
p002.s6.b0: Beauty may be seen in the physical universe and truth discerned in the intellectual world, but the goodness of God is found only in personal religious experience. The God of philosophy may be great and absolute, but the God of religion must be good. Man might fear a great God, but he trusts and loves only a good God.

head: Concept of God
Its fruits and its limits
rows: Fostered a high moral standard and a law-respecting people, but left the individual insecure
Father to Israel (the later Hebrew prophets)
A Father embracing the whole nation
The close family morality of parent and child—the entire mortal concept of God illuminated

p002.s6.b2.q: God loves not like a father, but as a father.

p002.s6.b3: From this standpoint the paper criticizes the atonement doctrine. To suppose that God’s righteousness cannot be reconciled with his love is to make him a divided personality, one of justice and one of mercy. But the Father needs no mediator in order to forgive; God as a father transcends God as a judge. God is never wrathful, vengeful, or angry.
p002.s6.b4: The saying “⟦Q 2:6.8⟧God loves the sinner and hates the sin⟦/Q⟧” is also made more precise here. Persons can love and hate only other persons, and sin is not a person. So the love of God saves the sinner, and the law of God destroys the sin. The goodness of God is the universal tendency to love, show mercy, manifest patience, and minister forgiveness.
p002.s7.h: VII. Divine Truth and Beauty — The Unity of Three Values
p002.s7.b0: The last section begins by teaching humility. All finite knowledge is relative; even information from high sources is only locally accurate and personally true. The philosopher’s gravest error is the “⟦Q 2:7.5⟧fallacy of abstraction⟦/Q⟧”—seizing one aspect of reality and declaring it the whole truth. Truth is beautiful because it is both replete and symmetrical.
p002.s7.b1: The section says that all things in the universe move toward unification. The physical universe coheres in the Isle of Paradise, the intellectual universe in the Conjoint Actor, and the spiritual universe in the personality of the Eternal Son. The isolated mortal of time and space coheres in God the Father through the indwelling Thought Adjuster. The Adjuster within us is a fragment of God that forever seeks divine unification.
p002.s7.b2: The section also points out what goes wrong when religion stresses goodness in isolation. The Hebrew religion failed to associate the goodness of God with the truths of science and the beauty of art, and the isolated morality of modern religion fails to hold the loyalty of many. The remedy is a new philosophy of living that gives equal consideration to truth, beauty, and goodness.

head: Value
Its quality
How it appears
rows: All truth—material, philosophic, or spiritual—is both beautiful and good
All real beauty—material art or spiritual symmetry—is both true and good
All genuine goodness—personal morality, social equity, or divine ministry—is true and beautiful

p002.s7.b4.q: Health, sanity, and happiness are integrations of truth, beauty, and goodness as they are blended in human experience.

p002.s8.b0: The God of Paper 2 is infinite yet draws near, perfect yet shares in our imperfection, righteous yet merciful. What binds all these qualities together is love, and that love has been given to us concretely in the Adjuster and in the life of Jesus. The paper shows that knowing God’s nature is closely tied to changing our own attitudes.

head: Practice
The teaching behind it
rows: When forgiving someone is hard, try to understand that person more deeply
The better we understand, the easier it is to forgive
On a day of failure, remember that God shares the experience
The Father participates in the experience of imperfection
Rather than trying to escape consequences, take care to sow well
Whatsoever a man sows, that shall he also reap
Approach God as a Father, not as a fearsome judge
Pursue truth, beauty, and goodness together
Their integration is health, sanity, and happiness

p002.s8.b2: Paper 3 goes on to the attributes of God—his omnipresence, omnipotence, omniscience, and more. If we read it remembering the “Father who is love” met in Paper 2, we will find that even those vast attributes are other faces of his love for his children.
p003.lead: God is everywhere present, all-powerful, and all-knowing: the paper that shows how these attributes touch our everyday lives.

p003.foot.text: Being the Divine Counselor assigned to the presentation of the revelation of the Universal Father

p003.s0.h: Introduction — The Attributes Converge in Fatherhood
p003.s0.b0: If Paper 2 portrayed God’s character, Paper 3 takes up his **attributes**: his everywhereness, infinite power, universal knowledge, limitlessness, supreme rule, and primacy. From the start the paper notes that the infinite Father is invisible, and that the ones who compensate for this invisibility are the Creator Sons. They are the personal expression of God to the children of time and space.
p003.s0.b1: The author is careful about ranking the attributes. Still, if one had to be put first, it would be creatorship. And that creatorship reaches its height in the truth that God is a Father. All the vast attributes this paper discusses point toward that single fact of fatherhood.

p003.s0.b2.q: And the creatorship of Deity culminates in the universal truth of the Fatherhood of God.

p003.s1.h: I. God’s Everywhereness — The Friend Within Our Own Heart
p003.s1.b0: God alone can be in numberless places at the same time. He is present in all parts and in all hearts of his creation, and it is literally true that God is all and in all. But the paper adds at once that while the cosmos reveals God, it cannot hold the whole of his infinity. The living God is immeasurably greater than the sum of creation.

p003.s1.b1.q: God is revealed throughout the cosmos, but the cosmos can never contain or encompass the entirety of the infinity of God.

p003.s1.b2: The warmest passage in this section is its confession that God lives in the creature. A paragraph gathering the sayings of ancient sages portrays God not as one far away but as part of us.

p003.s1.b3.q: Man goes forth searching for a friend while that very friend lives within his own heart.

p003.s1.b4: This presence is not untouched by our wrongdoing. The Thought Adjuster must go through the consequences of evil thinking together with the mind it indwells. So when we do wrong, we are in effect tormenting the gift of God within us.

head: Realm of presence
How God is present
rows: Potentially, in the gravity circuits of the Isle of Paradise—the primordial foundation of the coherence of material creation
Potentially, in the mind circuits of the Conjoint Actor and in the tensions of the Universal Absolute
Co-ordinated with the spirit presence of the Eternal Son and the potential of the Deity Absolute
The personality circuit and the Adjusters
God acts uniquely, directly, and exclusively

p003.s1.b6: This section also explains why God’s presence feels different from one person to another. Whether an Adjuster indwells a mind determines the fact of God’s presence, but his **effective presence** depends on how far that mind co-operates with the Adjuster. The Father does not withdraw because he has been slighted; his children, by their own choices, determine how far his influence reaches in their hearts.
p003.s2.h: II. God’s Infinite Power — A Power That Is Not Blind
p003.s2.b0: All the universes know that the Lord God omnipotent reigns. God is the primal cause of all physical phenomena; viewed as an unspiritual phenomenon, God is energy. He has ordained the circuits of all energy and decreed the time and manner in which energy-matter appears, and all of it is held in the gravity control centering on nether Paradise.
p003.s2.b1: Yet the weight of this section lies less in the size of God’s power than in its character. The Father is not a transient force or a fluctuating energy. When emergencies arise in human experience, he has already foreseen them all. When natural laws seem to be suspended or hastily corrected, it only looks that way because our view is so narrow.

p003.s2.b2.q: Regardless of appearances, the power of God is not functioning in the universe as a blind force.

p003.s2.b3: For the same reason, many of God’s acts seem arbitrary or even cruel to us. His doings consider the best good not only of one person or one planet but of all concerned. Since we are part of God’s family, we must sometimes share in the family discipline. And many things happen on the evolutionary worlds that are not the personal doings of the Father. This is an important teaching: we should not at once attribute suffering to the will of God.

head: What limits God’s power
In what way
rows: His infinite love, and truth, beauty, and goodness
His mercy ministry and fatherly relationship with the personalities of the universe
The righteousness and justice of the eternal Paradise Trinity

p003.s3.h: III. God’s Universal Knowledge — Down to a Single Sparrow
p003.s3.b0: God knows all things. The Universal Father is the only personality in all the universe who actually knows the number of the stars and planets of space. Quoting Jesus, the paper says that not one sparrow falls to the ground without the Father’s knowledge, and that the very hairs of our heads are numbered. God’s knowledge is supplemented indirectly through the divine Sons and directly through the indwelling Adjusters.

p003.s3.b1.q: Your Father knows what you have need of even before you ask him.

p003.s3.b2: If God knows everything in advance, what becomes of our freedom? The paper does not decide whether God chooses to foreknow events of sin. It says only that even if he does, such foreknowledge does not in the least abrogate his children’s freedom. Omnipotence, moreover, is not the power to do the ungodlike, and omniscience is not the knowing of the unknowable.

p003.s3.b3.q: One thing is certain: God is never subjected to surprise.

p003.s4.h: IV. God’s Limitlessness — Given Away, Yet Never Diminished
p003.s4.b0: The Father has given himself unstintingly to his Sons, his creations, and their countless creatures, yet he has lost nothing of what he possesses. However many new universes come into being, the controlling power of Paradise remains adequate; however freely mind is distributed to countless beings, the source of divine wisdom is not impoverished. Nor is there any limit to the number of Adjusters he can send.
p003.s4.b1: Finite man cannot think his way through God’s infinity. But here the paper offers a striking turn: that same finite human being can actually experience the full and undiminished impact of the infinite Father’s love. The quantity of that experience, however, is limited by our capacity for spiritual receptivity—our capacity to love the Father in return.

p003.s4.b2.q: Therefore man’s nearest and dearest approach to God is by and through love, for God is love.

p003.s5.h: V. The Father’s Supreme Rule — Why Uncertainty Is Needed
p003.s5.b0: In the creations beyond Havona the Father does not exercise his power directly; he rules through his Sons and their subordinate personalities. He acts independently only when a delegated personality fails in its trust. In the hearts of men the Father may not always have his way, but in the conduct and destiny of a planet the divine plan prevails.
p003.s5.b1: The heart of this section is its explanation that the uncertainties of life do not contradict God’s sovereignty. The author asks nine questions. Each virtue we desire can grow only in an environment where its opposite is possible.

head: The virtue desired
The environment it needs in order to grow
rows: Grappling with hardships and reacting to disappointments
A mind that ever knows less than it can believe
A world where error is present and falsehood always possible
An environment of relative goodness and beauty
The possibilities of betrayal and desertion
The incessant clamoring of the self for recognition and honor
A world where pain and suffering are ever-present possibilities

p003.s5.b3: Free intelligence cannot be uniformly wise from the beginning. So evolving man must be able to err if he is to be free. Yet the possibility of mistaken judgment is not in itself sin; it becomes sin only when the human will knowingly embraces a deliberate immoral judgment.

p003.s5.b4.q: evolving man must be fallible if he is to be free

p003.s5.b5: Comparing the perfect beings of Havona with mortals, the author shows the unique worth of our situation. The Havoners are what they are by virtue of the fact of existence, but everything divine that mortals gain is an experiential attainment.

p003.s5.b6.q: Everything divine which the human mind grasps and the human soul acquires is an experiential attainment

head: Virtue
Havona beings
Mortals
rows: Hope held with trust amid an uncertain world
Faith in the stability of the universe
Saving faith that lifts man from animal status to the portals of Paradise
The ecstasy of becoming an idealist by choice
An experience reached by the conquest of a belligerent self

p003.s6.h: VI. The Father’s Primacy — A Person, Not a Machine
p003.s6.b0: The Father delegates authority, but he reserves all final decisions. The universe is neither inevitable nor accidental; it is a work of creation and therefore wholly subject to the Creator’s will. And that will is divine truth and living love. The paper argues that universe causes cannot be lower than universe effects, and that man as a moral being cannot be explained unless the reality of the Universal Father is acknowledged.

p003.s6.b1.q: The will of God is divine truth, living love

p003.s6.b2: The remarks on the mechanistic philosopher are pointed. He rejects a sovereign will, yet that very will made the laws he so deeply reverences. To humanize God too much is a blunder, but to mechanize him completely is still more foolish.
p003.s6.b3: Asked whether the Father suffers, the author honestly answers that he does not know. The Creator Sons certainly can suffer, and he thinks the Father too experiences a fatherly and sympathetic understanding. God is power, pattern, and principle, but he is more: he is personal, and he shows a Father’s love to his children.

head: Deity
What he does for mankind
rows: Inspires the children of the universe to the ever-ascending adventure of finding the Father

p003.s7.b0: The attributes of Paper 3 sound distant and abstract, but they converge on a single fact: the One who is everywhere present, who knows all things, and who holds all power is our Father, and he lives within us. The paper also urges us not to read life’s uncertainties and pains as the absence of God, but as the soil in which virtues grow.

head: Practice
The teaching behind it
rows: Before seeking God far away, look within first
The friend already lives in our own heart
Increase your co-operation with the Adjuster to deepen God’s presence
His effective presence depends on the mind’s co-operation
Do not at once blame God for hardship
Many things occur that are not the Father’s personal doings
Treat uncertain situations as chances to grow courage and faith
Virtues grow where their opposites are possible
Come to the Father with trust instead of worry
He knows what we need before we ask

p003.s7.b2: Paper 4 goes on to God’s relation to the universe—how he deals with it, and the misunderstandings people have held about him. If we remember the attributes of Paper 3 as a Father’s attributes, the discussion of the next paper will feel much closer to home.
p004.lead: Providence and nature, the unchanging character of God, and the mistaken ideas of God that mankind has long held: the paper that sets them right.

p004.foot.text: Presented by a Divine Counselor of Uversa

p004.s0.h: Introduction — The Universe Has a Purpose
p004.s0.b0: Paper 4 deals with the relation God sustains to the universe. Its starting point is that the universe is not a machine rolling along without purpose. God created the universes of his own free and sovereign will, in accordance with an all-wise and eternal purpose, and he is executing that purpose throughout all time. The author humbly adds that it is doubtful whether anyone besides the Paradise Deities and their highest associates really knows very much about that eternal purpose.
p004.s0.b1: The perfect universe of Havona exists primarily for the pleasure and satisfaction of the Creators, while also serving as the pattern for all other universes and as the finishing school for pilgrims bound for Paradise. The ascension plan that perfects evolutionary mortals is one of the chief concerns of the superuniverses, but it is by no means the only occupation of the celestial hosts. This passage quietly invites us to let go of the idea that we are the center of the universe.

head: Havona’s purposes
What they are
rows: The pleasure and satisfaction of the perfect and infinite Creators
The model for all other universes
A place of training for the pilgrims of time on their way to Paradise

p004.s1.h: I. The Universe Attitude of the Father — What Providence Is
p004.s1.b0: The first section corrects misunderstandings about providence. Providence is real, but it is not the childish, arbitrary, and material ministry that many have imagined. It consists in the interlocking activities of celestial beings and divine spirits who, in accordance with cosmic law, labor for the honor of God and the spiritual advancement of his children. And providence and evolutionary progress are not in conflict.

p004.s1.b1.q: Can you not advance in your concept of God’s dealing with man to that level where you recognize that the watchword of the universe is progress?

p004.s1.b2: God is not one who created and then withdrew. If the Father should retire as the upholder of creation, there would immediately occur a universal collapse. The universe is constantly being renewed, and the Father unceasingly pours forth energy, light, and life. Even amid apparent instability, there is an underlying order and security.

p004.s1.b3.q: The universe is not wound up like a clock to run just so long and then cease to function

p004.s1.b4: In this section the Divine Counselor confesses that even he does not understand everything. He is well versed in the forces, minds, and spirits of the universes, yet he is constantly perplexed by the workings of the three Absolutes of potentiality. He explains the amazing co-ordination of apparently unrelated events as the living presence of the Supreme Being and the providential function of the Conjoint Actor. Much of what we call “accident” is, in the larger view, part of the drama the Infinite is unfolding.
p004.s2.h: II. God and Nature — Nature Is Not God
p004.s2.b0: Nature is, in a limited sense, the physical habit of God. God acts according to unchanging law throughout the master universe, but he modifies the patterns of his action to fit the evolutionary plans of each local universe and planet. On our world, moreover, the operation of those laws has been further affected by the errors and insurrections of beings belonging to our system of Satania.

head: Factor shaping nature
What it is
rows: The immutability, perfection, and rectitude of Paradise Deity
The experimental plans, executive blunders, insurrectionary errors, incompleteness of development, and imperfection of wisdom of extra-Paradise creatures
A nature stable underneath, yet of changing mood and varied from one local universe to another

p004.s2.b2: So the paper says that nature can never be a faithful portrayal of God. It mixes the perfect and the partial, and its face has been scarred by the rebellion and misconduct of myriads of creatures. To worship nature because God in some limited sense pervades it is a travesty.

p004.s2.b3.q: No, nature is not God. Nature is not an object of worship.

p004.s2.b4: Yet the defects of nature do not imply defects in God. The paper likens nature’s imperfections to the “stop-moments” in a moving reel of infinity picturization. It is these very interruptions that allow the finite mind to catch a fleeting glimpse of divine reality. God appears defective only when we look at nature with natural eyes, unaided by revelation. This is a viewpoint worth holding on to when disaster and suffering tempt us to doubt God’s goodness.
p004.s3.h: III. God’s Unchanging Character — Neither Jealous Nor Wrathful
p004.s3.b0: All too long has man thought of God as one like himself. God is jealous of no one. The sight of man bowing before his baser passions and his idols stirs God to be jealous **for** man, but never **of** him. Nor is God capable of wrath and anger in the human sense; such feelings are utterly foreign to the Father’s perfect nature.
p004.s3.b1: As a major reason for our difficulty in understanding God, the paper names the Lucifer rebellion and the Caligastia betrayal. On worlds not segregated by sin, the evolutionary races form far better ideas of the Father. Our distorted picture of God is bound up with the particular history of our planet.

head: Human wisdom
God’s wisdom
rows: Grows out of the trials and errors of experience
Consists in the perfection of infinite universe insight
Repents of nothing he has ever done
Grieves as a Father when his children fail to attain the levels they could reach

p004.s3.b3.q: God repents of nothing he has ever done, now does, or ever will do.

p004.s3.b4: The end of the section offers a clue to why relative evil exists. The Father’s infinite goodness is beyond the comprehension of finite minds, so relative goodness can be exhibited only in contrast with comparative evil. Here the paper is careful to add that this is not sin. And because God’s character is infinitely superhuman, it must be personalized, as in the divine Sons, before we can grasp it by faith.
p004.s4.h: IV. The Realization of God — Changeless but Not Immobile
p004.s4.b0: Since God is self-existent, he is absolutely independent and changeless. But this changelessness does not mean immobility. God can pass from simplicity to complexity, from infinity to finitude, from the divine to the human, modifying the manifestations of his absoluteness. This is possible because God is will.
p004.s4.b2: Personality and goodness God shares with other beings, but infinity of will is his alone. Yet the whole of his absolute nature is subject to the relationship of the Creator to his creature family. Trinitarian justice may be precise, but in his family relationship with the creatures of time God is governed by divine sentiment. That is why the author says that of all possible titles, he was instructed to portray God as the **Universal Father**.

head: Viewpoint
God is
rows: The one being who exists by himself, dependent on no other
Shows that this First Cause is the God of religion, full of mercy and goodness and pledged to the eternal survival of his children

p004.s4.b4: The paper says that God’s free will is neither ruled by power nor guided by intellect alone. The divine personality consists in spirit and shows itself to the universes as love. God’s tender nature finds its greatest satisfaction in loving and being loved. What we worship, too, is not the abstract concept of the Infinite but the experience-idea of God—our grasp of the personality and divinity of our highest concept of Deity.

p004.s4.b5.q: God is a Father in the highest sense of the term.

p004.s4.b6: This section sums up the victory of faith beautifully. Faced with the awful spectacle of human limitations, faith declares: even if I cannot do this, a part of the Father lives in me who can and will. That is the faith that overcomes the world.

p004.s4.b7.q: Even if I cannot do this, there lives in me one who can and will do it, a part of the Father-Absolute of the universe of universes.

p004.s5.h: V. Erroneous Ideas of God — No God Needs Appeasing
p004.s5.b0: The last section begins with the limits of religious tradition. Tradition is the imperfectly preserved record of the experiences of God-knowing people of past ages, and it has invariably been altered because primitive man was a mythmaker. Especially confusing has been the failure of sacred books to distinguish between different divine beings, gathering them all under the single name “God.”

head: Kind of confusion
What was mixed together
rows: Failure to distinguish clearly between the personalities of the Paradise Trinity
Between Paradise and the local universe
Failure to distinguish Paradise Deity from the local universe creators and administrators
Planetary Princes, System Sovereigns, Constellation Fathers, Creator Sons, Superuniverse Rulers, the Supreme Being, and the Universal Father all included under one appellation
Messages from Life Carriers and various orders of angels recorded as coming from God himself

p004.s5.b2: The gods who rampage in the storm, shake the earth in their wrath, and judge men with famine and flood are the gods of primitive religion, not the Gods who rule the universes. The same is true of the idea of appeasing an angry God through sacrifice, penance, and the shedding of blood. The paper declares it an affront to God to teach that innocent blood must be shed to win his favor. Yet it fairly acknowledges that Moses made a distinct advance when he forbade human sacrifice and substituted the sacrifice of animals.

p004.s5.b3.q: It is an affront to God to believe, hold, or teach that innocent blood must be shed in order to win his favor or to divert the fictitious divine wrath.

p004.s5.b4: In the same vein the paper explains Michael’s bestowal afresh. The bestowal was not needed to win God’s favor; it was inherent in the situation of closing a planetary age, and it was the final personal act of a Creator Son in earning the experiential sovereignty of his universe. The teaching that the Father’s mercy was withheld until he saw blood shed on the cross is a gross distortion of God’s character.

p004.s5.b5.q: But the inhabitants of Urantia are to find deliverance from these ancient errors and pagan superstitions respecting the nature of the Universal Father.

p004.s6.b0: Paper 4 helps us put in order the picture of God we carry in our minds. God has not left the universe but upholds it even now; he is not identical with nature; he is neither jealous nor wrathful; and he is no deity to be appeased with blood. He is will, and above all he is Father. The task this paper leaves us is to lay down the ideas of God born of fear and to receive the Father whom Jesus revealed.

head: Practice
The teaching behind it
rows: Drop the habit of reading disasters as God’s wrath
Gods who shake the earth in anger belong to primitive religion
Enjoy nature’s beauty, but give your worship to God
Nature is not an object of worship
Facing your limits, say, “The Father in me can do it”
The faith that overcomes the world
Leave room for a larger co-ordination even in “accidents”
Providence is the realm of the Supreme Being and the Conjoint Actor
Rather than striving to win God’s favor, respond to the love already given
The Father’s mercy is not bought with blood

p004.s6.b2: Paper 5 carries this line of thought forward to God’s relation to the individual. How the Father who upholds the universe draws near to each one of us, and how we in turn come to him, is the subject of the next paper.
p005.lead: How do we approach the infinite Father? The last paper of the Father series takes up the indwelling Adjuster, true worship, religion and God-consciousness, and the gift of personality.

p005.foot.text: The fifth and last of the series presenting the narrative of the Universal Father by a Divine Counselor of Uversa

p005.s0.h: Introduction — How Far Must We Go to Find God?
p005.s0.b0: The story of the Universal Father that began in Paper 1 comes down to the individual in Paper 5. How can so great a God have fellowship with a single person? The paper’s first answer is simple. An actual fragment of the living God, the Thought Adjuster, resides within every normal-minded and morally conscious mortal. Our assurance of divine fellowship must rest on this fact.

p005.s0.b1.q: Man does not have to go farther than his own inner experience of the soul’s contemplation of this spiritual-reality presence to find God and attempt communion with him.

p005.s0.b2: God has also reserved to himself the prerogative of bestowing personality and of maintaining direct, fatherly contact with all personal beings through the personality circuit. The Adjuster and the personality circuit—these two channels are the threads that run through the whole paper.
p005.s1.h: I. The Approach to God — The Way Is Open
p005.s1.b0: The finite creature cannot approach the Father directly, not because the Father is aloof, but because of our own finiteness. Were we transported to Paradise this very moment, we would not even know we were in the Father’s presence. Man must be spiritually translated many times. Yet apart from that long road, we can commune right now with the spirit of the Father within us.
p005.s1.b1: This section stresses equality of spiritual opportunity. People differ greatly in intellectual ability and social environment, but the possibilities for spiritual progress are equal to all. Everyone enjoys the same divine presence, has the same privilege of communing with that spirit, and can equally choose to accept its leading.

p005.s1.b2.q: To each of you and to all of us, God is approachable, the Father is attainable, the way is open

p005.s1.b3: What, then, hides God from us? The Father is not in spiritual hiding, but many creatures have hidden themselves in the mists of their own willful decisions. So long as the power of choice remains, a person may draw near God and may also turn away again and again. Final destiny is settled only when the desire to choose the Father’s will is lost forever—or when Adjuster fusion proclaims an irrevocable choice.

head: The crossroads
How it is determined
rows: While the power of choice remains—one may draw near or forsake the divine will
When the desire to know the Father and to be like him is finally and forever lost
When Adjuster fusion proclaims the final choice to live the Father’s will

p005.s2.h: II. The Presence of God — Known by Its Fruits
p005.s2.b0: God’s presence appears differently in different realms. His physical presence is the reality of the material universe; his mind presence depends on the depth of intellectual experience; his spiritual presence is differential, determined by spiritual receptivity and by the degree to which the will is consecrated to doing the divine will. And that presence is found most fully not in nature but in our attempted communion with the indwelling Adjuster.

p005.s2.b1.q: What a mistake to dream of God far off in the skies when the spirit of the Universal Father lives within your own mind!

p005.s2.b2: Many believers are uneasy because they do not clearly feel the Adjuster’s presence. The paper says that this in no way disproves the experience. It is exceedingly difficult for the material mind to be distinctly conscious of divine realities, and a new consciousness evolves as the soul grows. The proof of our relationship with the Adjuster is not a feeling but the **fruits of the spirit** borne in our lives.
p005.s3.h: III. True Worship — Adoration That Asks Nothing
p005.s3.b0: In the highest sense we worship the Universal Father and him only. We may worship the Father as he is manifested in his Creator Sons, but in the end it is the Father who is worshiped. This section draws a clear distinction between worship and prayer: worship is for its own sake, while prayer contains an element of self- or creature-interest.

p005.s3.b1.q: There is absolutely no self-request or other element of personal interest in true worship

p005.s3.b2: The moment self-interest intrudes, worship turns into prayer. Yet the paper adds that in practical religious life there is no reason why prayer should not be addressed to the Father as part of true worship. It then sorts out which Deity is concerned with the different parts of our lives.

head: What we do
The Deity and realm concerned
rows: The Universal Father—carried to him through the personality circuit
The Son—the realm of the Eternal Son and the Creator Son
The practical affairs of daily life
The Infinite Spirit—co-operating with spirit personalities of the Third Source and Center

p005.s3.b4: Worship is the mobilization of all the powers of the human personality under the dominance of the soul and the direction of the Adjuster. The mind consents to worship, the soul craves and initiates it, and the Adjuster conducts it on behalf of mind and soul. Worship thus becomes an experience that takes place on several levels at once.

p005.s3.b5.q: The spiritual growth of the soul takes place wholly independently of the intellectual self-consciousness.

head: Level on which worship is realized
Consciousness

p005.s4.h: IV. God in Religion — Many Paths and the Way of Jesus
p005.s4.b0: The religions of evolution drive people toward God by fear; the religions of revelation draw them to seek a God of love because they long to become like him. Religion, though, is not a passive feeling of dependence but a living and dynamic experience of divinity attainment predicated on service to humanity. The truly religious person does not bend the universe to serve the self but dedicates the self to the service of the universe family.

head: Religion
The salvation it offers and its focus
rows: Salvation from difficulties; prosperity predicated on righteousness · watchword “Know your God”
Salvation from disharmony and ugliness by the realization of beauty · watchword “Know yourself”
Salvation from sin; sanctity · “knowledge of the Lord Jesus Christ”
Deliverance from the rigorous moral standards of Judaism and Christianity
Salvation from self · “knowing God, and yourself as a son of God”

p005.s4.b2: The paper does not belittle the various religions. The morals of the Zoroastrians, the metaphysics of the Hindus, and the ethics of the Confucianists are all of value as valid approaches to the religion of Jesus. The Hebrews based their religion on goodness and the Greeks on beauty, but Jesus revealed a God of love, and love embraces truth, beauty, and goodness.

p005.s4.b3.q: The spiritual status of any religion may be determined by the nature of its prayers.

head: Concept merged into Christian theology
God is
rows: The vindicator of moral values, a righteous God
The unifier, a God of wisdom
A living friend, a loving Father, the divine presence

p005.s4.b5: Because these three streams were blended, Christian theology has found it hard to attain consistency. The paper urges us to view Jesus’ life positively—to think less of his sinlessness than of his righteousness and loving service. Jesus upstepped the passive love of the Hebrew concept to the active affection of a God who is the Father of every individual, even of the wrongdoer.
p005.s5.h: V. The Consciousness of God — No One Is Excluded
p005.s5.b0: Morality has its origin in the reason of self-consciousness, but that alone does not reach the spiritual level of religious experience. Religion is an independent realm, grounded neither in the facts of science nor in the obligations of society, and it may permeate the material, social, moral, and spiritual levels alike. The same God comes to the scientist as the First Cause, to the artist as the ideal of beauty, to the philosopher as universal unity, and to the believer as the loving Father.

head: Level of God-consciousness
What is realized
rows: The comprehension of the idea of God
The realization of the ideal of God
The realization of the spirit reality of God

p005.s5.b2: This section also treats the relation of faith and intellect with balance. The experience of God-consciousness stays the same from generation to generation, but the philosophic and theologic definitions of God must change with each advancing age. Religious experience must be willing to submit itself to intelligent criticism and reasonable interpretation; it must not seek to stand apart from the rest of human experience.
p005.s5.b3: The greatest comfort comes in the passage on the conditions of survival. Limits of intellect, lack of education and culture, or low social status cannot invalidate the presence of the divine spirit in a believing person. Just as parents need no diploma to have children, a mind that can discern right and wrong and worship God, united with an Adjuster, is enough to begin the growth of an immortal soul. What remains is the honest choice to seek God and do his will.

p005.s5.b4.q: When the mind believes God and the soul knows God, and when, with the fostering Adjuster, they all desire God, then is survival assured.

p005.s6.h: VI. The God of Personality — The Dignity of Free Will
p005.s6.b0: The Universal Father is the bestower and conservator of every personality and the destiny of all who choose to do his will. Personality is one of the unsolved mysteries of the universes. Neither mind nor spirit nor energy alone makes a personality; personality is a quality bestowed exclusively by the Father. Nor is it achieved by degrees: there either is personality or there is no personality.
p005.s6.b1: Having given personality and provided for the growth of an immortal soul, the Father stands aside. Whether to create the surviving, eternal self now rests with man’s own choice. No being or force in all the universe can interfere with that choice.

p005.s6.b2.q: As pertains to eternal survival, God has decreed the sovereignty of the material and mortal will, and that decree is absolute.

p005.s6.b3: Just as all gravity is circuited in the Isle of Paradise, all mind in the Conjoint Actor, and all spirit in the Eternal Son, so all personality is circuited in the personal presence of the Universal Father. This personality circuit unerringly carries the worship of all personalities to the Father. And the portal of eternity opens only in response to free-will choice. Closing the series, the author confesses that he can say nothing more helpful than this: God is our Father, and we are his children.

p005.s6.b4.q: No personal creature can be coerced into the eternal adventure

p005.s7.b0: Paper 5 is the conclusion of the Father series. The infinite Father lives within us as the Adjuster, knows us through the personality circuit, and absolutely respects our free choice. The way is open, and what we need to walk it is not learning or status but an honest desire to seek God and to become like him.
